other_game_info: Stage 1: one-shot simultaneous Prisoner’s Dilemma between Players A and B with 20-point endowment each; pass-all is doubled and given to partner (C) vs keep-all (D). CONFIG_defaultContribProp_reason: Each round they are “assigned an endowment of 20 tokens and decide whether they want to invest their tokens… or keep the tokens for themselves,” implying all 20 start in the private account.

CONFIG_chat_reason: No mention of communication or chat between participants.
CONFIG_showOtherSummaries_reason: End of each round: “each participant receives an overview of the results in both SI and SFI… contribution…, payoff…, assigned tokens…, received tokens…, and total round payoff.”

CONFIG_punishmentTech_reason: Same sentence: one negative token decreases target’s payoff by three tokens → 1:3.
CONFIG_rewardExists_reason: SI allows assigning positive tokens that increase others’ payoffs at 1:1.
CONFIG_rewardCost_reason: “Positive tokens increase the payoff… at a ratio of 1:1… Participants themselves lose the tokens they assigned…”, so each positive token costs 1.
CONFIG_rewardTech_reason: One positive token increases payoff of another participant by one token → 1:1.

other_game_info: Same indefinite repeated helping game and matching protocol as Baseline (four-person anonymous economies, random pairing each period, random seller/buyer roles). In addition, there is a constant supply of four intrinsically worthless electronic tickets per economy. In period 1 of each cycle, each buyer is endowed with two tickets; tickets can be carried over across periods within a cycle but not across cycles. Subjects can hold at most two tickets and cannot borrow. Ticket transfer is feasible only when the buyer has at least one ticket and the seller has fewer than two. Buyer’s action set when having tickets is {0 (keep), 1 (unconditional transfer), 1|Z (transfer conditional on cooperation)}; seller’s action set (unless holding two tickets) is {Y, Z, Z|1 (cooperate conditional on receiving one ticket)}. Choices are simultaneous, without communication, and only the outcome (Y or Z and whether a transfer occurred) is observed, not the opponent’s specific action. When conditional choices are incompatible, outcome is Y.
